working_title: What to Actually Look for in a Golf Rain Glove (and Why Your Normal Glove Is Letting You Down)
angle: Most UK club golfers play through wet conditions with a standard leather or synthetic glove and simply accept the loss of grip, not realising that dedicated rain gloves work on an opposite principle: they grip tighter the wetter they get. The post explains how rain gloves differ materially from all-weather and leather gloves, what features actually matter for UK conditions, and how to use them properly so they do their job.
research_notes:
- Standard cabretta leather gloves absorb water and lose friction when wet; rain gloves use synthetic materials (e.g. FiberSof, synthetic suede) that increase grip as moisture rises — the opposite behaviour
- Key brands/models in the 2026 UK market: FootJoy RainGrip (sold as a pair, long-standing go-to for UK golfers), MacWet Micromesh (worn by Aaron Rai regardless of conditions, known for grip-the-wetter-it-gets behaviour), TaylorMade Rain Control, Zero Restriction (premium/pricier end), Under Armour Drive Storm (part of AW 2024 range), Stuburt thermal gloves (for colder/wetter crossover)
- Rain gloves are typically sold in matched pairs (one per hand), unlike standard gloves sold individually — worth flagging as many club golfers don't realise this
- MacWet gloves: Aaron Rai wore them at the 2020 Scottish Open during Storm Alex, cited by Today's Golfer as their year-round winter choice
- FootJoy RainGrip described as 'the go-to wet-weather glove for UK golfers for years' (moresports.com, 2026)
- Practical care tip: after a wet round, remove and reshape the glove, air-dry away from direct heat; rotating between two gloves extends life (thegolfshoponline.co.uk)
- All-weather synthetic gloves (e.g. FootJoy WeatherSof) sit in a middle ground — fine for drizzle, but not optimised for heavy rain the way a dedicated rain glove is
- Rain gloves can feel slightly cold in prolonged rain and are less suited to frequent on/off during a round — relevant for golfers who remove their glove to putt
- Keeping a spare all-weather glove plus a dedicated rain pair covers most UK conditions year-round
